newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down but pare some losses toward close.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down but pare some losses toward close.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended lower on Wednesday after paring some losses in late trade due to a Finance Ministry official's comments about interest rates.
The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) current low interest rate policy still has positive effects on the economy, Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The comment led to some short-covering, but once things calmed down, people realised it was not such a big factor," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The September ended at 126.10, down from the previous day's close of 126.50. Turnover was 43,550 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.160 percent as of 0629 GMT, up from Tuesday's close of 2.115 percent.
"We believe the effects of the low rate (policy) are spreading to various sectors (of the economy). It still has positive effects," MOF's Komura said in an interview.
He added that policy on the official discount rate (ODR) was solely in the hands of the BOJ and refrained from commenting on the outlook for the ODR.
The September rose to around 126.20 from 126.08 after Komura's comments reached the market, but fell again toward the close.

"Long liquidation, by dealers who built up long positions in the morning when the September made a try for the upside, probably took place and dragged down the September toward the end," the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Traders said the weakness of JGBs was mainly due to technical factors.
"JGBs are in a correction phase following a runaway rise," a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.

"The JGB market has entered a correction after the benchmark JGB yield fell to a record low (on Monday), and position adjustment sales, profit-taking and long-liquidation are now taking place," the second trader said.
Investors' buying on dips, which had supported the market earlier, was not as prevalent as before, the first trader said.
"Buying on dips was seen, but such demand was not as strong as it has been recently," the first trader said.
Investors' bargain-hunting also seems to be coming in at a lower price level than before, a city bank trader said.

"Investors are targeting a lower price level for their bargain-hunting than before, and now seem intent on buying when the price for the September is between 126.00 to 126.10," a city bank trader said.
JGBs fell in morning trade partly on talk of cash JGB selling by a city bank and selling of non-JGB issues by an agricultural financial institution.
Sentiment was also dampened as loss-cut selling of JGBs appeared once Tokyo share prices came off their morning lows, traders said.
